catalog_quote: Muklom has three tone categories (see also Mulder 2018b), which are indicated in transcriptions by superscript numbers 1, 2, and 3 following the syllable. A superscript zero indicates tonelessness ... [3.2.2 Stress] With respect to prosody, the TB languages are divided into two areas: a northern region which has trochaic stress, and a south-eastern region with iambic stress (LaPolla 2017a:51). ... A portion of the Muklom lexicon consists of so-called sesquisyllabic words. ... In Muklom, the order of syllables is minor-major, so the language falls under the group of languages which show iambic stress. An example of a sesquisyllabic word is /tʰʌ0ɹɔk/ 'six'. The first syllable contains a schwa-like short vowel and carries no tone even though it concerns a non-stopped syllable. The minor syllable in a sesquisyllabic word is always open, i.e. V or CV. ... audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: all quoted fragments found verbatim in the Mulder 2020 text we hold at pp. 65, 66, 71-72 and 83, matching the record's locators. (2) Deciding source is a 2020, 496-page descriptive grammar (PhD, La Trobe) by the sole specialist on Muklom; Glottolog has no descriptive refs for the languoid and web search finds no later or instrumental prosody study. The grammar itself flags the stress section as 'a first exploration' and says phonological-word stress 'remains to be established' (sect. 4.4), which the record's the primary-stress rule already reflects ('No stress rule is given for words composed of full syllables'). (3) downloaded van Dam 2018 (La Trobe PhD on Tangsa-Nocte tone) independently confirms lexical tone in Muklom (sect. 8.6) and states group-wide that presyllables are 'toneless and unstressed' (p. 94), i.e. the same iambic-sesquisyllable picture; Morey 2019 and Mulder 2016 are silent on

sources.quote: p. 94: 'Tangsa-Nocte varieties typically have lexical tone. Aside from the presence of semi-syllables, forming what is referred to in Matisoff (2003) as sesquisyllables, Tangsa-Nocte is a group of what can be reffered to as monsyllabic language varieties. ... The presyllable is toneless and unstressed, and in certain lexical items may be a reduced form of a tonal morpheme'. p. 229: 'Muklom has a lexical tone system similar to other Tangsa-Nocte varieties ...
